subtopics.title: Swachh Vayu Diwas and Clean Air Day
subtopics.summary: Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 7 September 2026 and coincides with the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies. The International Day was designated by the UN General Assembly in 2019 and carries the 2026 theme 'Clean Air for Climate Action'. The occasion marked the presentation of the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards.
facts: Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 7 September 2026.
It coincides with the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.
The UN General Assembly designated the International Day in 2019.
The 2026 theme of the International Day is 'Clean Air for Climate Action'.
India observes the occasion as Swachh Vayu Diwas.
The occasion marked presentation of the 5th Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards.

subtopics.title: National Clean Air Programme and NCAP targets
subtopics.summary: The National Clean Air Programme was launched by MoEFCC in 2019 as a national-level strategy covering 130 non-attainment cities along with million-plus cities. Its first target was a 20-30 per cent cut in PM10 and PM2.5 by 2024 using 2017 as the baseline, later enhanced to a 40 per cent cut in particulate matter by 2026. The revised target has not been fully achieved, as only 26 of 130 cities recorded a reduction of 40 per cent or more.
facts: NCAP was launched by MoEFCC in 2019 as a national-level strategy.
NCAP covers 130 non-attainment cities along with million-plus cities.
Non-attainment cities are those that failed to comply with NAAQS over a specified assessment period.

Target was enhanced to a 40% reduction in particulate matter concentration by 2026.

In 2025-26, 108 cities recorded reductions in annual PM10 compared to 2017-18.

subtopics.title: Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan and city rankings
subtopics.summary: The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan was launched in 2022-23 as an annual assessment of the 130 NCAP cities. Cities are grouped into three population categories and evaluated across five key parameters. The 2026 edition introduced ward-level rankings for the first time, and the city-level toppers in each category are listed in the booklet.
facts: Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan was launched in 2022-23 as an annual assessment of 130 NCAP cities.
Cities are grouped as Category I (above 10 lakh), Category II (3-10 lakh) and Category III (below 3 lakh).
Cities are evaluated on Ambient Air Quality, Source Apportionment, Action Plan Implementation, Institutional Capacity and Public Participation.
Category I (2026): Lucknow 1st (198), Indore 2nd (197), Jabalpur 3rd (195).
Category I bottom 5: Chennai, Jamshedpur, Kota, Kolkata and Madurai.
Delhi ranked 30th in Category I.
Category II (2026): Rourkela 1st (198.5); Firozabad and Guntur joint 2nd (195); Amravati 3rd (194).
Category III (2026): Kalinganagar 1st (198.5); Angul 2nd (196.5); Talcher 3rd (193.5).
The 2026 edition introduced Ward-level Rankings for the first time.

subtopics.title: Pollution control tools, measures and laws
subtopics.summary: The booklet lists monitoring tools, field measures, emergency action and legal provisions against air pollution. Monitoring includes the National Air Quality Index and SAFAR, while field measures include the Turbo Happy Seeder and Pusa Bio-Decomposer. The legal base includes the Air Act 1981, Water Act 1974 and Environment Protection Act 1986, along with Article 51A(g) and Article 21.
facts: National Air Quality Index (2014) is a tool for communicating air quality status in easy terms.
Turbo Happy Seeder can uproot stubble and also sow seeds in the area cleared.
Pusa Bio-Decomposer turns crop residue into manure in 15-20 days and was developed by IARI.
Graded Response Action Plan (2017) is a set of emergency measures.
GRAP measures kick in only when air quality shifts from Poor to Very Poor.
SAFAR is a Ministry of Earth Sciences initiative to monitor city-wide and localised air quality.
Bharat Stage VI (2020) made the leap from BS-IV to BS-VI mandatory nationwide.
Air Act 1981, Water Act 1974 and Environment Protection Act 1986 are key pollution control regulations.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) inserted Clause (g) in Article 51A, making protection of the natural environment a Fundamental Duty.
Article 21 has been interpreted to include the right to a healthy environment.

quizzes.title: Sarvekshan rankings check
quizzes.passage: The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan is an annual assessment of the cities covered under the National Clean Air Programme. It was first launched in 2022-23. The cities are grouped into three categories according to their population: Category I covers the largest cities, Category II covers mid-sized cities and Category III covers the smallest cities in the assessment. The assessment focuses on seven areas of measures: road dust management, solid waste management, vehicular emissions, industrial emissions, construction and demolition waste, commercial sources, and public awareness and outreach initiatives. Cities are evaluated on five key parameters: ambient air quality, source apportionment, action plan implementation, institutional capacity and public participation. Swachh Vayu Diwas 2026 was observed on 7 September 2026, which coincides with the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies. The fifth set of Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards was presented on that occasion. The awards recognise cities and wards that have shown effective air pollution mitigation measures under the programme. The 2026 edition also introduced a new feature: ward-level rankings, which show how individual wards compare with one another. City-level results are reported within each category, which means cities are compared with others of similar population.

quizzes.title: NCAP numbers check
quizzes.passage: The National Clean Air Programme is a national-level strategy launched by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to address air pollution through coordinated interventions across sectors. It covers non-attainment cities along with million-plus cities. Non-attainment cities are those that have failed to comply with the National Ambient Air Quality Standards over a specified assessment period. Its initial target was a 20 to 30 per cent reduction in PM10 and PM2.5 concentrations by 2024. Later, the target was enhanced to a reduction in particulate matter concentration by 2026, and the revised target has not been fully achieved. Annual PM10 concentrations are compared with the base year to measure progress. Progress is also tracked through the PRANA portal, which was launched to track NCAP progress and regulate air pollution in non-attainment cities. The National Air Quality Index is a tool for communicating air quality status to people in terms that are easy to understand. The Graded Response Action Plan is a set of emergency measures that come into effect when air quality shifts from Poor to Very Poor. Other measures include the Bharat Stage VI vehicle emission standards, which replaced BS-IV norms nationwide.
